WITH patient_ratios AS (
    SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.HGB / NULLIF(l.HCT, 0)) AS ratio
    FROM Laboratory AS l
    WHERE l.HGB IS NOT NULL AND l.HCT IS NOT NULL AND l.HCT <> 0
    GROUP BY l.ID
), overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(ratio) AS overall_avg
    FROM patient_ratios
), above_overall AS (
    SELECT p.ID, p.ratio, p.ratio - o.overall_avg AS above_overall
    FROM patient_ratios AS p
    CROSS JOIN overall AS o
    WHERE p.ratio > o.overall_avg
), group_avg AS (
    SELECT AVG(ratio) AS group_avg
    FROM above_overall
), final_patients AS (
    SELECT a.ratio, a.above_overall, a.ratio - g.group_avg AS above_group
    FROM above_overall AS a
    CROSS JOIN group_avg AS g
    WHERE a.ratio > g.group_avg
)
SELECT AVG(ratio) AS average_ratio,
       AVG(above_overall) AS average_amount_above_overall,
       AVG(above_group) AS average_amount_above_group
FROM final_patients;

assumptions.assumption: Each patient's ratio is the average of their per-test HGB/HCT ratios, excluding tests with a missing HGB or HCT and zero HCT; the overall and group averages give each patient equal weight.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat each lab test as an observation, calculate its HGB/HCT ratio, and use test-level averages and filtering throughout.
